candidates.change_summary: Remove the overflow assertion so deposit always adds msg.value without checking for overflow.
Delete the balance increment so deposited ether is not recorded.
Change the asserted overflow check to always fail (assert(false)), making deposit always revert.
Delete the require statement so that withdrawals can exceed the balance.
Delete the balance decrement so the sender's balance remains unchanged after withdrawal.
Delete the transfer so that no Ether is sent while the balance is still reduced.
Replace the require condition to check creator instead of sender balance.
Move the balance decrement before the transfer, making the contract vulnerable to reentrancy.
Replace 'payable(to).transfer(address(this).balance)' with 'payable(creator).transfer(address(this).balance)' to send the contract balance to the creator instead of the `to` address.
Replace 'require(creator == msg.sender)' with 'require(creator != msg.sender)' so the require condition fails for the creator but passes for others, altering who can call migrateTo successfully.
Delete the require statement so anyone can call migrateTo and transfer the contract balance to any address.
Replace 'address(this).balance' with '0' so migrateTo transfers 0 ether instead of the contract's balance.
Insert 'selfdestruct(payable(to));' before the require statement, destroying the contract and sending balance to `to` unconditionally.

Replace 'payable(to).transfer(address(this).balance)' with 'payable(to).transfer(address(this).balance + 1)' to transfer one wei more than the actual balance (will revert due to insufficient balance unless contract somehow has extra balance from another source).
Insert 'balances[msg.sender] = address(this).balance;' after the require statement, corrupting the balances mapping before the transfer.
Move the require statement after the transfer, so the transfer occurs unconditionally and the require check happens only afterward.
